subject.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context

question: Should OpenClaw accept the custom cooperative glob walker and bootstrap-hook scheduling as the bounded fix for the reported bootstrap-context stalls despite possible ordering, prompt-byte, and session-timing differences?
rationale: The implementation is a focused, well-proven response to a P1 runtime stall, but bootstrap files and hook execution are compatibility-sensitive context surfaces whose permanent semantics require owner intent.

options.title: Refresh And Land
options.body: Resolve the current conflicts, rerun exact-head bootstrap and SDK checks, and accept the remaining internal compatibility tradeoff.

options.title: Require Full Embedded-Run Proof
options.body: Keep the implementation shape but request a current-head live embedded-run or channel-latency transcript before accepting the risk.

options.title: Pause For Runtime Redesign
options.body: Hold or close the PR if maintainers prefer worker isolation, priority scheduling, or caching over this focused cooperative mitigation.
